Ch. 4 // Talk Eight // The Great Financial Scandal of 2003
An account by Charles T. Munger

The Great Financial Scandal of 2003二〇〇三年的金融大丑闻

The great financial scandal erupted in 2003 with the sudden, deserved disgrace of Quant Technical Corporation,305Quant Technical CorporationQuant技术公司 always called Quant Tech. By this time, Quant Tech was the country’s largest pure engineering firm, having become so as a consequence of the contributions of its legendary founder, engineer Albert Berzog Quant.

2003年，随着宽特技术公司（Quant Technical Corporation，305Quant Technical CorporationQuant技术公司人们向来称之为宽特科技（Quant Tech））突遭理应降临的声名扫地，那场金融大丑闻骤然爆发。其时，宽特科技已是全国最大的纯工程企业，这全赖其传奇创始人——工程师阿尔伯特·贝索格·宽特（Albert Berzog Quant）——的贡献所致。

After 2003, people came to see the Quant Tech story as a sort of morality play divided into two acts. Act I, the era of the great founding engineer, was seen as a golden age of sound values. Act II, the era of the founder’s immediate successors, was seen as the age of false values, with Quant Tech becoming, in the end, a sort of latter-day Sodom or Gomorrah.

2003年之后，人们开始把宽特科技的故事视作一出分为两幕的道德剧。

“After 2003, people came to see the Quant Tech story as a sort of morality play divided into two acts.”2003 年之后，人们开始把 Quant Tech 的故事看作一出分为两幕的道德剧。

In fact, as this account will make clear, the change from good to evil did not occur all at once when Quant Tech’s founder died in 1982. Much good continued after 1982, and serious evil had existed for many years prior to 1982 in the financial culture in which Quant Tech had to operate.

事实上，正如本篇记述将要阐明的，从善到恶的转变并非在宽特科技创始人1982年离世时骤然发生。1982年之后，许多良善依然延续；而在1982年之前的许多年里，宽特科技不得不置身其中的金融文化里，严重的恶早已存在。

The Quant Tech story is best understood as a classic sort of tragedy in which a single flaw is inexorably punished by remorseless Fate. The flaw was the country’s amazingly peculiar accounting treatment for employee stock options. The victims were Quant Tech and its country. The history of the Great Financial Scandal, as it actually happened, could have been written by Sophocles.306Sophocles

(496–406 BC), an ancient Greek playwright, dramatist, priest, and politician of Athens, is best known as one of the three great Greek tragedians (the others being Aeschylus and Euripides, with whom he often competed in dramatic contests). Sophocles wrote over 100 plays; many scholars, including Aristotle, considered him to be the greatest playwright in ancient Greek theater. The most famous of his surviving works are the tragedies of Oedipus Rex and

索福克勒斯（Sophocles，公元前 496–前 406 年）是古希腊的剧作家、戏剧家、祭司和雅典政治家，最为人知的身份是三大希腊悲剧作家之一（另两位是埃斯库罗斯和欧里庇得斯，他常与他们在戏剧比赛中同台竞技）。索福克勒斯写了一百多部剧作；包括亚里士多德在内的许多学者都认为他是古希腊剧场最伟大的剧作家。他现存最著名的作品是悲剧《俄狄浦斯王》（Oedipus Rex）和……

要理解宽特科技的故事，最好把它当作一出经典的悲剧：剧中，一个单方面的瑕疵遭到无情命运女神毫不留情的惩罚。这个瑕疵便是该国对职工股票期权令人惊异的奇特会计处理。受害者是宽特科技及其国家。这场金融大丑闻的真实历史，简直可以由索福克勒斯（Sophocles）执笔写成。

As his life ended in 1982, Albert Berzog Quant delivered to his successors and his Maker a wonderfully prosperous and useful company. The sole business of Quant Tech was designing, for fees, all over the world, a novel type of superclean and superefficient small power plant307Small power plant小型发电厂 that improved electricity generation.

1982年，阿尔伯特·贝索格·宽特的生命走到尽头时，他向继任者和他的造物主交付了一家极为繁荣而有作为的公司。宽特科技惟一的业务，是面向全球、收取费用，设计一种新颖的、超级清洁又超级高效的小型发电厂，以改善电力供应。

By 1982, Quant Tech had a dominant market share in its business and was earning $100 million on revenues of $1 billion. Its costs were virtually all costs to compensate technical employees engaged in design work. Direct employee compensation cost amounted to 70 percent of revenues. Of this 70 percent, 30 percent was base salaries and 40 percent was incentive bonuses being paid out under an elaborate system designed by the founder. All compensation was paid in cash. There were no stock options because the old man considered the accounting treatment required for stock options to be “weak, corrupt, and contemptible,” and he no more wanted bad accounting in his business than he wanted bad engineering. Moreover, the old man believed in tailoring his huge incentive bonuses to precise performance standards established for individuals or small groups instead of allowing what he considered undesirable compensation outcomes, both high and low, such as he believed occurred under other companies’ stock option plans.

到1982年，宽特科技在其业务领域已占据统治性市场份额，在10亿美元营收的基础上赚取1亿美元利润。它的成本几乎全都是支付给从事设计工作的技术员工的报酬。直接的员工薪酬成本占营收的70%。在这70%当中，30%是基本工资，40%是依创始人设计的一套精密体系发放的激励奖金。所有薪酬均以现金支付。公司没有股票期权，因为这位老人认为股票期权所要求的会计处理“软弱、腐败且可鄙”，他既不愿意在自己的企业里做糟糕的账目，正如他不愿意做糟糕的工程设计。此外，这位老人信奉将巨额激励奖金精确挂钩于为个人或小组设定的绩效标准，而不愿放任他认为不可取的、过高或过低的薪酬结果——他认为那种结果正出现在其他公司的股票期权计划之下。

他既不愿意在自己的企业里做糟糕的账目，正如他不愿意做糟糕的工程设计。

“He no more wanted bad accounting in his business than he wanted bad engineering.”他绝不容许自己生意里有糟糕的会计，正如他绝不容许糟糕的工程。

Yet even under the old man’s system, most of Quant Tech’s devoted longtime employees were becoming rich, or sure to get rich. This was happening because the employees were buying Quant Tech stock308Quant tech stockQuant科技股票 in the market, just like nonemployee shareholders. The old man had always figured that people smart enough and self-disciplined enough to design power plants could reasonably be expected to take care of their own financial affairs in this way. He would sometimes advise an employee to buy Quant Tech stock, but more paternalistic than that he would not become.

然而，即便在老人的制度之下，宽特科技那些忠心耿耿的老员工大多也已变得富裕，或注定会富裕起来。原因在于，这些员工和公司以外的股东一样，在市场上买入宽特科技的股票。老人向来认为，既然员工聪明到、自律到足以设计发电厂，便大可合理地指望他们以这种方式打理好自己的财务。他偶尔会建议某位员工买入宽特科技的股票，但家长式的关怀也仅止于此，他不会更进一步。

By the time the founder died in 1982, Quant Tech was debt-free and, except as a reputation enhancer, really didn’t need any shareholders’ equity to run its business, no matter how fast revenues grew. However, the old man believed with Ben Franklin that “it is hard for an empty sack to stand upright,” and he wanted Quant Tech to stand upright. Moreover, he loved his business and his coworkers, and he always wanted to have on hand large amounts of cash equivalents so as to be able to maximize work-out or work-up chances if an unexpected adversity or opportunity came along. And so, in 1982, Quant Tech had on hand $500 million in cash equivalents, amounting to 50 percent of revenues.

到1982年创始人离世时，宽特科技已无任何债务；除了作为声誉的加持，无论营收增长多快，它的经营其实都不需要任何股东权益。然而，老人与本杰明·富兰克林（Ben Franklin）一样相信“空袋子难以直立”，而他希望宽特科技能够巍然直立。此外，他热爱自己的事业与同仁，总希望手头持有大量现金等价物，以便在不期而遇的困境或机遇来临时，能够最大限度地把握脱困或发展的机会。于是，1982年宽特科技手中持有5亿美元的现金等价物，相当于营收的50%。

Possessing a strong balance sheet and a productive culture and also holding a critical mass of expertise in a rapidly changing and rapidly growing business, Quant Tech, using the old man’s methods, by 1982 was destined for 20 years ahead to maintain profits at 10 percent of revenues while revenues increased at 20 percent per year. After these 20 years, commencing in 2003, Quant Tech’s profit margin would hold for a very long time at 10 percent while revenue growth would slow down to 4 percent per year. But no one at Quant Tech knew precisely when its inevitable period of slow revenue growth would begin.

凭借稳健的资产负债表、富有成效的文化，以及在快速变化、快速增长的行业中掌握的关键性专业知识，沿用老人的方法，到1982年宽特科技注定要在未来20年里将利润维持在营收的10%，而营收每年增长20%。这20年之后，自2003年起，宽特科技的利润率将在很长时间内保持在10%，而营收增速将放缓至每年4%。但宽特科技内部无人能确切预知那段不可避免的营收低速增长期究竟何时开启。

The old man’s dividend policy for Quant Tech was simplicity itself: He never paid a dividend. Instead, all earnings simply piled up in cash equivalents.

老人为宽特科技制定的分红政策本身再简单不过：他从不派发股息。相反，所有盈利只是堆积在现金等价物里。

老人为宽特科技制定的分红政策本身再简单不过：他从不派发股息。相反，所有盈利只是堆积在现金等价物里。

Earnings piling up
“The old man’s dividend policy for Quant Tech was simplicity itself: He never paid a dividend. Instead, all earnings simply piled up in cash equivalents.”老人为 Quant Tech 定的分红政策简单至极：他从不分红。相反，所有盈利都堆成了现金等价物。

Every truly sophisticated investor in common stocks could see that the stock of cash-rich Quant Tech provided a splendid investment opportunity in 1982, when it sold at a mere 15 times earnings and, despite its brilliant prospects, had a market capitalization of only $1.5 billion. This low market capitalization, despite brilliant prospects, existed in 1982 because other wonderful common stocks were also then selling at 15 times earnings or less as a natural consequence of high interest rates then prevailing, plus disappointing investment returns that had occurred over many previous years for holders of typical diversified portfolios of common stocks.

每一位真正老练的普通股投资者都能看出，1982年现金充裕的宽特科技股票提供了一个绝佳的投资机会——当时它的市盈率仅为15倍，尽管前景辉煌，市值却只有15亿美元。这种尽管前景光明、市值却偏低的情形之所以出现在1982年，是因为其他优秀的普通股当时也同样以15倍或更低市盈率交易，这自然而然是当时高利率，加上此前多年典型多元化普通股组合持有者所获投资回报令人失望的结果。

One result of Quant Tech’s low market capitalization in 1982 was that it made Quant Tech’s directors uneasy and dissatisfied right after the old man’s death. A wiser board would then have bought in Quant Tech’s stock very aggressively, using up all cash on hand and also borrowing funds to use in the same way. However, such a decision was not in accord with conventional corporate wisdom in 1982. And so the directors made a conventional decision. They recruited a new CEO and CFO from outside Quant Tech, in particular from a company that had a conventional stock option plan for employees and also possessed a market capitalization at 20 times reported earnings, even though its balance sheet was weaker than Quant Tech’s and its earnings were growing more slowly than earnings at Quant Tech. Incident to the recruitment of the new executives, it was made plain that Quant Tech’s directors wanted a higher market capitalization as soon as feasible.

宽特科技1982年的低市值所造成的一个后果，是让董事会在老人刚一离世便感到不安与不满。若是一个更明智的董事会，本会极其激进地回购宽特科技的股票，用尽手头所有现金，并再借入资金如法炮制。然而，这样的决定并不符合1982年通行的企业智慧。于是董事们作出了一个常规的决定：他们从宽特科技之外——尤其从一家实行常规员工股票期权计划的公司——聘来新的首席执行官（CEO）和首席财务官（CFO）；那家公司市值高达报表利润的20倍，尽管其资产负债表不如宽特科技强健，盈利增速也慢于宽特科技。在延揽新高管的过程中，董事们清楚地表明，他们希望尽快提高宽特科技的市值。

The newly installed Quant Tech officers quickly realized that the company could not wisely either drive its revenues up at an annual rate higher than the rate in place or increase Quant Tech’s profit margin. The founder had plainly achieved an optimum in each case. Nor did the new officers dare tinker with an engineering culture that was working so well. Therefore, the new officers were attracted to employing what they called “modern financial engineering,”310Modern financial engineering

One of the most famous examples of modern financial engineering was the Ponzi scheme, which started in Boston in 1919. Claiming an ability to exploit an unforeseen arbitrage in international postal coupons, Carlo “Charles” Ponzi attracted thousands of investors by promising 50 percent interest in 90 days. To build credibility, he used funds from recent investors to provide returns to earlier participants—a standard pyramid scheme tactic. Soon, Ponzi had taken in millions. In 1920, The Boston Post ran a story questioning Ponzi’s practices, which provoked an independent audit. The audit revealed the fraud, and investors demanded their money back. In the end, the average participant had only 37 percent of invested funds returned, and Ponzi spent several years in prison. Unrepentant, Ponzi turned up again in the late 1920s selling worthless land in Florida.

现代金融工程最著名的例子之一是庞氏骗局，它 1919 年始于波士顿。卡洛“查尔斯”·庞兹（Carlo “Charles” Ponzi）声称自己有能力利用国际邮政礼券中一个未曾预见的套利机会，承诺 90 天 50% 的利息，吸引了数千名投资者。为建立信誉，他用新投资者的钱向早期参与者支付回报——这是金字塔骗局的标准手法。很快，庞兹就吸纳了数百万美元。1920 年，《波士顿邮报》（The Boston Post）刊出一篇质疑庞兹手法的报道，由此引发了一次独立审计。审计揭穿了骗局，投资者纷纷要求拿回自己的钱。最终，普通参与者只收回了投入资金的 37%，庞兹则在狱中度过数年。毫无悔改之意的庞兹，20 世纪 20 年代末又出现在佛罗里达，推销毫无价值的土地。

which required prompt use of any and all arguably lawful methods for driving up reported earnings, with big, simple changes to be made first.

新上任的宽特科技高管很快意识到，公司既不可能明智地将营收年增速提升到现有水平之上，也无法提高宽特科技的利润率。创始人在这两方面显然都已臻于至善。新高管也不敢去摆弄那套运转良好的工程文化。因此，他们被吸引去采用所谓“现代金融工程311Financial engineering金融工程”——即须迅速动用一切堪称合法的手法来推高报表利润，先从重大而简单的改动做起。

By a strange irony of fate, the accounting convention for stock options that had so displeased Quant Tech’s founder now made the new officers’ job very easy, and would ultimately ruin Quant Tech’s reputation. There was now an accounting convention in the United States that, provided employees were first given options, required that when easily marketable stock was issued to employees at a below-market price, the bargain element for the employees, although roughly equivalent to cash, could not count as a compensation expense in determining a company’s reported profits. This amazingly peculiar accounting convention had been selected by the accounting profession, over the objection of some of its wisest and most ethical members, because corporate managers, by and large, preferred that their gains from exercising options covering their employers’ stock not be counted as an expense in determining their employers’ earnings.

命运弄人，那个曾令宽特科技创始人如此不快的股票期权会计惯例，如今却让新高管的活儿变得十分轻松，并最终将毁掉宽特科技的声誉。当时美国有一项会计惯例：只要先授予员工期权，那么当可轻易变现的股票以低于市价的价格发行给员工时，员工所获得的折让部分——尽管几乎等同于现金——在核算公司报表利润时，却不能计入薪酬费用。这项令人惊异的奇特会计惯例，是在该行业一些最睿智、最讲道德的成员反对之下，由会计行业选定的，因为企业管理者大体上都不希望自己行权其雇主股票所获的收益，在核算雇主盈利时被计为费用。

The accounting profession, in making its amazingly peculiar decision, had simply followed the injunction so often followed by persons quite different from prosperous, entrenched accountants. The injunction was that normally followed by insecure and powerless people: “Whose bread I eat, his song I sing.” Fortunately, the income tax authorities did not have the same amazingly peculiar accounting idea as the accounting profession. Elementary common sense prevailed, and the bargain element in stock option exercises was treated as an obvious compensation expense, deductible in determining income for tax purposes.

会计行业在作出这项惊异的奇特决定时，不过是奉行了一句常被那些与优裕稳固的会计师截然不同的人所遵从的箴言。那句箴言通常是缺乏安全感、无权无势的人所遵循的：“谁给我面包吃，我就为谁唱歌。”所幸，所得税主管机关并未抱持与会计行业相同的惊异奇特之见。起码的常识占了上风，期权行权中的折让部分被视为显而易见的薪酬费用，在计算应税所得时予以扣除。

“Whose bread I eat, his song I sing.”吃谁的面包，就唱谁的歌。

Quant Tech’s new officers, financially shrewd as they were, could see at a glance that, given the amazingly peculiar accounting convention and the sound income tax rules in place, Quant Tech had a breathtakingly large opportunity to increase its reported profits by taking very simple action. The fact that so large a share of Quant Tech’s annual expense was incentive bonus expense provided a modern financial engineering311Financial engineering金融工程 opportunity second to none.

宽特科技的新高管虽说在财务上精明过人，却一眼看出：凭着这项惊异奇特的会计惯例，再加上健全的所得税规则，宽特科技只需采取极其简单的行动，便有令人咋舌的巨大机会来抬高其报表利润。宽特科技年度开支中竟有如此之大的一份是激励奖金支出，这为“现代金融工程”提供了无与伦比的良机。

For instance, it was mere child’s play for the executives to realize that if in 1982 Quant Tech had substituted employee stock option exercise profits for all its incentive bonus expenses of $400 million, while using bonus money saved plus option prices paid to buy back all shares issued in option exercises, and keeping all else the same, the result would have been to drive Quant Tech’s 1982 reported earnings up by 400 percent, to $500 million from $100 million, while shares outstanding remained exactly the same! And so it seemed that the obviously correct ploy for the officers was to start substituting employee stock option exercise profits for incentive bonuses. Why should a group of numerate engineers care whether their bonuses were in cash or virtually perfect equivalents of cash? Arranging such substitutions, on any schedule desired, seemed like no difficult chore.

举例而言，高管们轻而易举便想通了：倘若在1982年，宽特科技用员工股票期权行权获利替换掉全部4亿美元的激励奖金支出，同时用省下的奖金加上员工支付的期权价款，回购所有因行权而发行的股份，其余一切保持不变，其结果将是把宽特科技1982年的报表利润从1亿美元推高400%，达到5亿美元，而流通股数量分毫未变！于是，对高管们而言，显然正确的伎俩便是着手以员工股票期权行权获利替换激励奖金。一群懂数字的工程师，何必在乎自己的奖金是现金，还是近乎完美的现金等价物？按任何想要的节奏安排这种替换，似乎都不是难事。

However, it was also mere child’s play for the new officers to realize that a certain amount of caution and restraint would be desirable in pushing their new ploy. Obviously, if they pushed their new ploy too hard in any single year, there might be rebellion from Quant Tech’s accountants or undesirable hostility from other sources. This, in turn, would risk killing a goose with a vast ability to deliver golden eggs,312Golden eggs金蛋 at least to the officers. After all, it was quite clear that their ploy would be increasing reported earnings only by adding to real earnings an element of phony earnings—phony in the sense that Quant Tech would enjoy no true favorable economic effect (except a temporary fraud-type effect similar to that from overcounting closing inventory) from that part of reported earnings increases attributable to use of the ploy. The new CEO privately called the desirable, cautious approach “wisely restrained falsehood.”

然而，新高管同样轻而易举地意识到，在推行这一新伎俩时，一定程度的谨慎与克制是十分可取的。显然，若在某一年把新伎俩推得太狠，宽特科技的会计人员可能会反叛，其他方面也可能报以不受欢迎的敌意。这反过来又会冒着杀死一只能下大量金蛋的鹅的风险——至少对高管们而言如是。毕竟，他们很清楚，自己的伎俩之所以能抬高报表利润，无非是在真实盈利之上附加了一层虚假盈利——所谓虚假，是指宽特科技从这部分因使用该伎俩而增加的报表利润中，不会获得任何真正有利的经济效果（除了一种类似于多计期末存货造成的临时性欺诈式效应）。新任CEO私下把这种可取而谨慎的做法称作“明智克制的谎言”。

新任CEO私下把这种可取而谨慎的做法称作“明智克制的谎言”。

“The new CEO privately called the desirable, cautious approach ‘wisely restrained falsehood.’”新任 CEO 私下把那种可取的、审慎的做法称作『明智克制的谎言』。

Plainly, the new officers saw, it would be prudent to shift bonus payments to employee stock option exercise profits in only a moderate amount per year over many years ahead. They privately called the prudent plan they adopted their “dollop-by-dollop system,” which they believed had four obvious advantages:

新高管们显然看出，审慎之举是在未来许多年里，每年只将奖金支付适度地转为员工股票期权行权获利。他们私下把所采纳的这项审慎计划称为“一勺一勺制”，并相信它有四个明显的优点：

First, a moderate dollop of phony earnings in any single year would be less likely to be noticed than a large dollop.

第一，任何单一年份里适度的一勺虚假盈利，比一大勺更不易被察觉。

Second, the large long-term effect from accumulating many moderate dollops of phony earnings over the years would also tend to be obscured in the dollop-by-dollop system. As the CFO pithily and privately said, “If we mix only a moderate minority share of turds with the raisins313Raisins葡萄干 each year, probably no one will recognize what will ultimately become a very large collection of turds.”

第二，在“一勺一勺制”下，经年累月积攒许多适度虚假盈利所形成的大幅长期效应，也倾向于被掩盖。正如那位CFO精辟而私下所言：“倘若我们每年只在葡萄干里掺入一小撮屎，大概没人会认出那最终将变成的一大堆屎。”

“If we mix only a moderate minority share of turds with the raisins each year, probably no one will recognize what will ultimately become a very large collection of turds.”倘若我们每年只在葡萄干里掺入少量、少量的粪块，大概没人会察觉，那最终会积累成一大堆粪块。

Third, the outside accountants, once they had blessed a few financial statements containing earnings increases, only a minority share of which were phony, would probably find it unendurably embarrassing not to bless new financial statements containing only the same phony proportion of reported earnings increases.

第三，外部会计师一旦为几份包含盈利增长、且其中仅有少数为虚假的财务报表背书，若新财务报表所含的报表盈利增长中虚假比例完全相同，他们大概会觉得不予背书将令人难堪至极。

Fourth, the dollop-by-dollop system would tend to prevent disgrace, or something more seriously harmful, for Quant Tech’s officers. With virtually all corporations except Quant Tech having ever-more liberal stock option plans, the officers could always explain that a moderate dollop of shift toward compensation in option-exercise form was needed to help attract or retain employees. Indeed, given corporate culture and stock market enthusiasm likely to exist as a consequence of the strange accounting convention for stock options, this claim would often be true.

第四，“一勺一勺制”往往有助于防止宽特科技高管身败名裂，或遭受更严重的伤害。由于除宽特科技外，几乎所有公司都实行越来越宽松的股票期权计划，高管们总可以解释：适度向期权行权形式的薪酬偏移一勺，是为了帮助吸引或留住员工。的确，考虑到因股票期权的奇特会计惯例而很可能存在的企业文化与股市热情，这种说法往往属实。

With these four advantages, the dollop-by-dollop system seemed so clearly desirable that it only remained for Quant Tech’s officers to decide how big to make their annual dollops of phony earnings. This decision, too, turned out to be easy. The officers first decided upon three reasonable conditions they wanted satisfied:

有了这四个优点，“一勺一勺制”显得如此明确可取，宽特科技高管只需决定每年舀出多大的虚假盈利之勺。这个决定同样被证明很容易。高管们首先确定了三条他们希望得到满足的合理条件：

First, they wanted to be able to continue their dollop-by-dollop system without major discontinuities for 20 years.

第一，他们希望“一勺一勺制”能够连续不断地施行20年，不出现重大中断。

Second, they wanted Quant Tech’s reported earnings to go up by roughly the same percentage each year throughout the whole 20 years, because they believed that financial analysts representing institutional investors would value Quant Tech’s stock higher if reported annual earnings growth never significantly varied.

第二，他们希望在整个20年里，宽特科技的报表盈利每年都以大致相同的百分比增长，因为他们相信，若报表年度盈利增长从不出现显著波动，代表机构投资者的金融分析师会给宽特科技股票更高的估值。

Third, to protect credibility for reported earnings, they never wanted to strain the credulity of investors by reporting, even in their 20th year, that Quant Tech was earning more than 40 percent of revenues from designing power plants.

第三，为维护报表盈利的可信度，他们绝不愿让投资者的信任承受重压——即便在第20年，也不愿报表显示宽特科技从设计发电厂中赚取超过营收40%的利润。

With these requirements, the math was easy, given the officers’ assumption that Quant Tech’s non-phony earnings and revenues were both going to grow at 20 percent per year for 20 years. The officers quickly decided to use their dollop-by-dollop system to make Quant Tech’s reported earnings increase by 28 percent per year instead of the 20 percent that would have been reported by the founder.

有了这些要求，数学便很简单——前提是高管们假定宽特科技的非虚假盈利与营收在未来20年里都将每年增长20%。高管们很快决定动用“一勺一勺制”，让宽特科技的报表盈利每年增长28%，而非创始人本本会报出的20%。

And so, the great scheme of modern financial engineering went forward toward tragedy at Quant Tech. And few disreputable schemes of man have ever worked better in achieving what was attempted. Quant Tech’s reported earnings, certified by its accountants, increased regularly at 28 percent per year. No one criticized Quant Tech’s financial reporting except a few people widely regarded as impractical, overly theoretical, misanthropic cranks. It turned out that the founder’s policy of never paying dividends, which was continued, greatly helped in preserving credibility for Quant Tech’s reports that its earnings were rising steadily at 28 percent per year. With cash equivalents on hand so remarkably high, the Pavlovian314Pavlovian

Ivan Pavlov (1849–1936) was born in central Russia and attended seminary until age 21, when he abandoned theology in favor of chemistry and physiology. Earning his MD in 1883, he excelled in physiology and surgical techniques. Later, he studied the secretory activity of digestion and ultimately formulated the laws of conditioned reflexes. Pavlov’s most famous experiment showed that dogs tend to salivate before food is actually delivered to their mouths. This result led him to a long series of experiments in which he manipulated the stimuli occurring before the presentation of food. He thereby established the basic laws for the establishment and extinction of what he called “conditional reflexes,” later mistranslated from the original Russian as “conditioned reflexes.” He was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1904 for his work on digestive secretions.

伊万·巴甫洛夫（Ivan Pavlov，1849–1936 年）生于俄罗斯中部，在神学院读到 21 岁，随后弃神学而选化学和生理学。1883 年他获得医学博士学位，在生理学和外科手术技艺上表现出色。后来，他研究消化液的分泌活动，最终归纳出条件反射的规律。巴甫洛夫最著名的实验表明，狗在食物真正送到嘴边之前就会开始分泌唾液。这一结果引导他进行了一长串实验，在实验中他操控食物呈现之前发生的刺激，从而为他所谓的“条件反射”（conditional reflexes，该词后来由俄语原意误译为 conditioned reflexes）的建立与消退确立了基本规律。1904 年，他因消化液研究获诺贝尔奖。

mere-association effects that so often impair reality recognition served well to prevent detection of the phony element in the reported earnings.

于是，这项现代金融工程的宏大方案朝着宽特科技的悲剧推进。人类干过的不光彩勾当中，鲜有比这更胜一筹、更能达成其图谋的。经会计师认证的宽特科技报表盈利，规规矩矩地每年增长28%。除了少数被普遍视为不切实际、过度理论化、愤世嫉俗的怪人，无人批评宽特科技的财务报告。结果证明，创始人从不派发股息的政策得到了延续，极大地有助于维护宽特科技“盈利每年稳健增长28%”这一报表的可信度。由于手头现金等价物高得惊人，那种常常损害现实认知的巴甫洛夫式纯粹联想效应，很好地阻止了人们察觉报表盈利中的虚假成分。

于是，这项现代金融工程的宏大方案朝着宽特科技的悲剧推进。

“And so, the great scheme of modern financial engineering went forward toward tragedy at Quant Tech.”于是，现代金融工程那套宏大方案，在 Quant Tech 朝着悲剧一路推进。

It was therefore natural, after the dollop-by-dollop system had been in place for a few years, for Quant Tech’s officers to yearn to have Quant Tech’s reported earnings per share keep going up at 28 percent per year while cash equivalents grew much faster than they were then growing. This turned out to be a snap. By this time, Quant Tech’s stock was selling at a huge multiple of reported earnings, and the officers simply started causing some incremental stock option exercises that were not matched either by reductions in cash bonuses paid or by repurchases of Quant Tech’s stock.

因此，在“一勺一勺制”施行数年之后，宽特科技高管自然会渴望让报表每股收益继续以每年28%攀升，同时让现金等价物以远快于当时的速度增长。这被证明轻而易举。此时宽特科技股票正以报表盈利的超高倍数交易，高管们干脆开始催生一些增量式的股票期权行权，而既不同步削减所支付的现金奖金，也不同步回购宽特科技的股票。

This change, the officers easily recognized, was a very helpful revision of their original plan. Not only was detection of the phony element in the reported earnings made much more difficult as cash accumulation greatly accelerated, but also a significant amount of Ponzi scheme or chain-letter effect was being introduced into Quant Tech, with real benefits for present shareholders, including the officers.

高管们轻易便认识到，这一改动对他们原计划是极有帮助的修订。随着现金积累大幅加速，报表盈利中虚假成分被察觉的难度大大提高了；不仅如此，宽特科技还被注入了大剂量的庞氏骗局或连锁信效应，给包括高管在内的现有股东带来了实实在在的好处。

At this time, the officers also fixed another flaw in their original plan. They saw that as Quant Tech’s reported earnings, containing an increasing phony element, kept rising at 28 percent, Quant Tech’s income taxes as a percentage of reported pretax earnings kept going lower and lower. This plainly increased their chances of attracting undesired questions and criticism. This problem was soon eliminated. Many power plants in foreign nations were built and owned by governments, and it proved easy to get some foreign governments to raise Quant Tech’s design fees, provided that in each case slightly more than the fee increase was paid back in additional income taxes to the foreign government concerned.

此时，高管们还修补了原计划的另一处漏洞。他们发现，随着宽特科技报表盈利（含日益增长的虚假成分）持续以28%攀升，其所得税占报表税前盈利的比例却越来越低。这显然增加了招致不受欢迎的质疑与批评的可能。这个问题很快被消除。许多外国的发电厂由政府修建并所有，结果很容易说服一些外国政府提高宽特科技的设计费，条件是每次都将略高于费用增幅的部分，以额外所得税的形式返还给相关外国政府。

Finally, for 2002, Quant Tech reported $16 billion in earnings on $47 billion in revenue that now included a lot more revenue from interest on cash equivalents than would have been present without net issuances of new stock over the years. Cash equivalents on hand now amounted to an astounding $85 billion, and somehow it didn’t seem impossible to most investors that a company virtually drowning in so much cash could be earning the $16 billion it was reporting. The market capitalization of Quant Tech at its peak early in 2003 became $1.4 trillion, about 90 times earnings reported for 2002.

最后，在2002年，宽特科技报表利润为160亿美元，营收470亿美元；这营收中来自现金等价物利息的部分，比历年若无净发行新股时所能有的要多得多。手头现金等价物如今达到惊人的850亿美元，而对多数投资者来说，一家几乎被如此巨量现金淹没的公司能赚到它所报表的160亿美元，似乎也并非不可能。2003年初宽特科技市值见顶时达到1.4万亿美元，约为其2002年报表利润的90倍。

However, all man’s desired geometric progressions, if a high rate of growth is chosen, at last come to grief on a finite Earth. And the social system for man on earth is fair enough, eventually, that almost all massive cheating ends in disgrace. And in 2003, Quant Tech failed in both ways.

然而，人类所向往的一切几何级数增长，只要选定了高增速，最终都会在这颗有限的地球上走向悲局。而地球上的人类社会终究足够公正，几乎一切大规模的欺诈都以身败名裂收场。2003年，宽特科技在两方面双双失败。

人类所向往的一切几何级数增长，只要选定了高增速，最终都会在这颗有限的地球上走向悲局。

“All man’s desired geometric progressions, if a high rate of growth is chosen, at last come to grief on a finite Earth.”人类所有心仪的几何级数增长，一旦选定高增长率，终将在这颗有限的地球上撞上灾祸。

By 2003, Quant Tech’s real earning power was growing at only 4 percent per year after sales growth had slowed to 4 percent. There was now no way for Quant Tech to escape causing a big disappointment for its shareholders, now largely consisting of institutional investors. This disappointment triggered a shocking decline in the price of Quant Tech stock, which went down suddenly by 50 percent. This price decline, in turn, triggered a careful examination of Quant Tech’s financial reporting practices, which, at long last, convinced nearly everyone that a very large majority of Quant Tech’s reported earnings had long been phony earnings, and that massive and deliberate misreporting had gone on for a great many years. This triggered even more price decline for Quant Tech stock until in mid-2003 the market capitalization of Quant Tech was only $140 billion, down 90 percent317Down 90 percent下跌90% from its peak only six months earlier.

到2003年，在销售增速放缓至4%之后，宽特科技真实的盈利能力每年仅增长4%。此时宽特科技已无法避免让其股东——如今主要已是机构投资者——大失所望。这一失望触发了宽特科技股价的惊人下跌，骤然下挫50%。股价的下跌反过来又触发了对宽特科技财务报告操作的仔细审查，最终几乎说服了所有人：宽特科技报表利润中的绝大部分长久以来都是虚假盈利，而大规模、蓄意的错报已持续了许多年。这又引发了宽特科技股价更大幅度的下跌，直到2003年年中，其市值仅剩1400亿美元，较仅仅六个月前的峰值下跌了90%。

A quick 90 percent decline in the price of the stock of such an important company that was previously so widely owned and admired caused immense human suffering, considering the $1.3 trillion in market value that had disappeared. And naturally, with Quant Tech’s deserved disgrace, the public and political reaction included intense hatred and revulsion directed at Quant Tech, even though its admirable engineers were still designing the nation’s best power plants.

这样一家曾广受持有与推崇的重要公司，其股价在短期内暴跌90%，考虑到1.3万亿美元市值凭空蒸发，给人们带来了巨大的苦难。而理所当然地，随着宽特科技罪有应得的声名扫地，公众与政界的反应中充满了对宽特科技的强烈憎恨与反感，尽管它那些令人钦佩的工程师仍在设计全国最好的发电厂。

Moreover, the hatred and revulsion did not stop with Quant Tech. It soon spread to other corporations, some of which plainly had undesirable financial cultures different from Quant Tech’s only in degree. The public and political hatred, like the behavior that had caused it, soon went to gross excess and fed upon itself. Financial misery spread far beyond investors into a serious recession like that of Japan in the 1990s following the long period of false Japanese accounting.

此外，憎恨与反感并未止于宽特科技。它很快蔓延到其他企业，其中有些显然拥有不良的金融文化，与宽特科技的区别只在程度。公众与政界的憎恨，正如引发它的那种行为一样，很快就走向极度失控，并自我助长。金融苦难远远超出投资者范围，演成一场严重的衰退，如同20世纪90年代日本在长期的虚假会计之后所经历的那样。

There was huge public antipathy to professions following the Great Scandal. The accounting profession, of course, got the most blame. The rulemaking body for accountants had long borne the acronym FASB, and now nearly everyone said this stood for “Financial Accounts Still Bogus.”

大丑闻之后，公众对各行各业的专业人士充满了极大的反感。会计行业自然挨了最多的骂。会计师的规则制定机构长久以来以缩写FASB（财务会计准则委员会）著称，如今几乎人人都说这代表着“财务报告依然做假”（Financial Accounts Still Bogus）。

会计师的规则制定机构长久以来以缩写FASB（财务会计准则委员会）著称，如今几乎人人都说这代表着“财务报告依然做假”（Financial Accounts Still Bogus）。

“The rulemaking body for accountants had long borne the acronym FASB, and now, nearly everyone said this stood for ‘Financial Accounts Still Bogus.’”会计师的准则制定机构久以缩写 FASB 著称，而如今，几乎人人都说它代表『财务报表依然造假』（Financial Accounts Still Bogus）。

Economics professors, likewise, drew much criticism for failing to blow the whistle on false accounting and for not sufficiently warning about the eventual bad macroeconomic effects of widespread false accounting. So great was the disappointment with conventional economists that Harvard’s John Kenneth Galbraith318John Kenneth Galbraith

John Kenneth Galbraith (1908–2006) , born in Ontario, Canada, graduated from Ontario Agricultural College and went on for a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. In 1949, he joined the economics faculty at Harvard University. A friend of President John F. Kennedy, Galbraith served as US ambassador to India from 1961 to 1963. As an economist, Galbraith held progressive values and wrote accessible books that often describe how economic theory does not always mesh with real life. Among his best-known works are American Capitalism: The Concept of Countervailing Power (1952), The Affluent Society (1958), and The New Industrial State (1967).

约翰·肯尼斯·加尔布雷思（John Kenneth Galbraith，1908–2006 年）生于加拿大安大略，毕业于安大略农学院，后从加州大学伯克利分校获得博士学位。1949 年，他加入哈佛大学经济学教师队伍。作为肯尼迪总统的朋友，加尔布雷思 1961 年至 1963 年出任美国驻印度大使。作为经济学家，加尔布雷思秉持进步价值观，写的书通俗易懂，常常描述经济理论并不总能与现实生活吻合。他的名著包括《美国资本主义：抗衡力量的概念》（American Capitalism: The Concept of Countervailing Power，1952）、《丰裕社会》（The Affluent Society，1958）和《新工业国》（The New Industrial State，1967）。

received the Nobel Prize in economics. After all, he had once predicted that massive, undetected corporate embezzlement would have a wonderfully stimulating effect on the economy. And people could now see that something very close to what Galbraith had predicted had actually happened in the years preceding 2003 and had thereafter helped create a big, reactive recession.

经济学教授们同样招致诸多批评，因为他们未能对虚假会计吹响警哨，也未能充分警示普遍存在的虚假会计最终将给宏观经济带来的恶劣后果。对传统经济学家的失望如此之深，以至于哈佛大学的约翰·肯尼思·加尔布雷斯（John Kenneth Galbraith）荣获了诺贝尔经济学奖。毕竟他曾预言，大规模、未被察觉的公司侵吞行为会对经济产生绝妙的刺激效应。人们如今可以看出，与加尔布雷斯所预言极为相近的情形，确实在2003年之前的那些年里发生了，并随后助长了一场巨大的、报复性的衰退。

With Congress and the SEC so heavily peopled by lawyers, and with lawyers having been so heavily involved in drafting financial disclosure documents now seen as bogus, there was a new lawyer joke every week. One such was: “The butcher says, ‘The reputation of lawyers has fallen dramatically,’ and the checkout clerk replies, ‘How do you fall dramatically off a pancake?’”

But the hostility to established professions did not stop with accountants, economists, and lawyers. There were many adverse “rub-off” effects on the reputations of professionals who had always performed well, like engineers, who did not understand the financial fraud that their country had made a conventional requirement. In the end, much that was good about the country and needed for its future felicity was widely and unwisely hated.

但是，对既有专业人士的敌意并未止于会计师、经济学家和律师。许多向来表现良好的专业人士——比如工程师——的声誉也受到了不利的“牵连”效应，他们并不理解自己的国家已把那种金融欺诈变成了一种常规要求。到头来，这个国家许多美好、且为其未来福祉所必需的事物，遭到了广泛而不明智的憎恨。

At this point, action came from a Higher Realm. God himself, who reviews all, changed His decision schedule to bring to the fore the sad case of the Great Financial Scandal of 2003. He called in his chief detective and said, “Smith, bring in for harsh but fair judgment the most depraved of those responsible for this horrible outcome.”

此时，行动来自更高的境界。洞悉一切的上帝本人改变了他的裁决日程，将2003年金融大丑闻这桩可悲案子提上日程。他召来首席侦探，说道：“史密斯（Smith），去把那些对这一可怕结局负有责任、最为堕落的人带上来，接受严厉而公正的审判。”

But when Smith brought in a group of security analysts who had long and uncritically touted the stock of Quant Tech, the Great Judge was displeased. “Smith,” he said, “I can’t come down hardest on low-level cognitive error, much of it subconsciously caused by the standard incentive systems of the world.”

可是，当史密斯带进来一群长期不加批判地吹捧宽特科技股票的证券分析师时，大法官不悦了。“史密斯，”他说，“我不能对低层次的认知错误施加最严厉的惩罚，它们大半是由世间标准的激励体系在潜意识中造成的。”

Next, Smith brought in a group of SEC commissioners and powerful politicians. “No, no,” said the Great Judge, “these people operate in a virtual maelstrom of regrettable forces and can’t reasonably be expected to meet the behavioral standard you seek to impose.”

接着，史密斯带进来一群SEC委员与权势熏天的政客。“不，不，”大法官说，“这些人运作于一团由令人遗憾的力量组成的、近乎迷宫般的漩涡之中，实在不能合理地指望他们达到你所试图强加的行为标准。”

Now the chief detective thought he had gotten the point. He next brought in the corporate officers who had practiced their version of modern financial engineering at Quant Tech. “You are getting close,” said the Great Judge, “but I told you to bring in the most depraved. These officers will, of course, get strong punishment for their massive fraud and disgusting stewardship of the great engineer’s legacy. But I want you to bring in the miscreants who will soon be in the lowest circle in Hell, the ones who so easily could have prevented all this calamity.”

这时首席侦探自以为明白了。他接着带进来那些在宽特科技推行其版本“现代金融工程”的公司高管。“你接近了，”大法官说，“但我让你带的是最为堕落的人。这些高管当然会因他们大规模的欺诈、以及对那位伟大工程师遗产令人作呕的托管而受到重罚。但我要你带的是那些很快将被打入地狱最底层的恶徒——那些本可以轻而易举阻止这场大灾难的人。”

At last, the chief detective truly understood. He remembered that the lowest circle of Hell was reserved for traitors. And so he now brought in from Purgatory a group of elderly persons who, in their days on earth, had been prominent partners in major accounting firms.

首席侦探终于真正明白了。他想起地狱最底层是留给叛徒的。于是，他如今从炼狱带进来一群老者，他们在尘世之日曾是各大会计师事务所显赫的合伙人。

“Here are your traitors,” said the chief detective. “They adopted the false accounting convention for employee stock options. They occupied high positions in one of the noblest professions, which, like yours, help make society work right by laying down the right rules. They were very smart and securely placed, and it is inexcusable that they deliberately caused all this lying and cheating that was so obviously predictable. They well knew what they were doing was disastrously wrong, yet they did it anyway. Owing to the press of business in Your Judicial System, you made a mistake at first in punishing them so lightly. But now you can send them into the lowest circle in Hell.”

“这就是你要的叛徒，”首席侦探说。“他们采纳了针对员工股票期权的虚假会计惯例。他们在最高尚的职业之一身居高位，那个职业与你的职分相似，都是通过确立正确的规则来帮助社会正常运转。他们极为聪明、地位稳固，却故意造成了这一切明显可预见的谎言与欺骗，实属不可原谅。他们十分清楚自己的所作所为是灾难性的错误，却依然故我。由于您的司法系统事务繁忙，您起初对他们处罚过轻，犯了一个错误。但现在您可以把他们打入地狱最底层了。”

Startled by the vehemence and presumption, the Great Judge paused. Then He quietly said, “Well done, my good and faithful servant.”

大法官被这番激烈言辞与大胆妄为惊得一怔，停顿片刻。然后他轻声说道：“做得好，我良善又忠心的仆人。”

This account is not an implied prediction about 2003. It is a work of fiction. Except in the case of Professor Galbraith, any resemblance to real persons or companies is accidental. It was written in an attempt to focus possibly useful attention on certain modern behaviors and belief systems.

本篇记述并非对2003年的隐含预言。它是一篇虚构作品。除加尔布雷斯教授一事外，任何与真实人物或公司的相似之处均属偶然。它写就的初衷，是试图将可能有用的注意力聚焦于某些现代行为与信仰体系。
